newsitem.title: HONG KONG: April's Riaupulp in talks with bondholders.
newsitem.headline: April's Riaupulp in talks with bondholders.

text.p: PT Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper (Riaupulp) said on Wednesday that it will enter into discussions with significant bondholders regarding a potential mandatory redemption of notes.
Riaupulp is a subsidiary of Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings Ltd (April).

At issue is a controversial, mandatory redemption of US$100 million in guaranteed secured notes due 2000 and US$200 million in guaranteed secured notes due 2005 of Riaupulp financing entity RAPP International Finance.

Indenture forms on the US$300 million of outstanding Yankee bonds oblige Riaupulp to retire all of its outstanding secured debt at 101 percent of the principal amount if collateral sales exceed 25 percent of the book value of the collateral.
The redemption clause was triggered by Riaupulp's decision to sell a power plant and a chemical manufacturing facility.
The chemical plant will be sold to another April company, PT Indorayon Utama.
Bondholders have charged that the sales are unneccessary and were entered into solely to trigger the redemption of the bonds so that Riaupulp could refinance more cheaply.
At the time of the announcement in January, the Yankee bonds were trading well above the redemption price.
Riaupulp said Wednesday that it had told bondholders in a conference call after the January announcement that it was open to comments.

"As part of this process and in the interest of preserving the goodwill Riaupulp has with its investors, management is arranging to meet with them to continue its ongoing dialogue and to evaluate what may be a mutually beneficial and amicable resolution to the issue," Riaupulp said in today's statement.

Riaupulp, which has maintained that it has done nothing wrong in calling the issue and has simply adhered to the bond contract, said that it currently has no specific proposals and would probably be discussing a number of potential alternatives with bondholders.
Franklin Templeton is thought to be the largest holder of the RAPP bonds, with some US$25-30 million.
